implementation: Optional AM_EARLY_API experiment using unmodified MinHook v1.3.4

recovery: external hooks removed then lease expired

design: Reject covered target application calls to foreground activation before entering user32.
Keep window-message input. Do not falsify GetFocus/GetForegroundWindow results.
Preserve the foreground thread keyboard-focus HWND; allow private background queue focus required by controls.
Do not use CBT veto in early API mode.
Expire the guard when the system last-input timestamp changes; do not protect unrelated UI threads.
A repeated ShowWindow request on an already visible protected window is suppressed; hidden-window restoration is not provided.
negativeEvidence: Initial Qt positive-control focus check assumed an exact child HWND; Qt can focus the root. The query now recognizes root or the expected child, while the independent foreground-thread focus assertion remains exact.

Initial Qt layer checks failed. Instrumentation showed the cover order had changed before guarded input, during initial module installation/settling. The harness establishes and asserts its measured baseline after installation without activation; the post-input order assertion is retained.
limits: After the user restored WeChat through its own UI, three scoped conversation switches passed; see the separate live acceptance record. This is not full mailbox or new-process coverage.
No keyboard events were generated. Focus ownership was checked through GetGUIThreadInfo(0), not through an actual typing test.
Human takeover timestamp handling is implemented but not yet tested with physical concurrent input.
New windows/processes, other UI threads and additional activation APIs are not covered.
Inactive detours and a module reference remain until the disposable target exits; production unload is not implemented.
